unit.why: A brief anecdote: as a child in Lublin, the subject was pointed out by the Seer of Lublin, who foretold that in his days Judah and Jerusalem would be saved; the narrator adds that because of our sins it did not come about.
unit.boundary_note: one of a numbered series of short anecdotes about the same figure (grandson of the Kozienice Maggid); the previous and next divisions are separate anecdotes

stories.end_quote: תוושע יהודה וירושלים, ובעונותינו שרבו כו׳
stories.summary_en: When the subject was a child in Lublin, the Seer of Lublin pointed at him and declared that in his days Judah and Jerusalem would be saved, a promise the narrator laments went unfulfilled because of the generation's sins.

tags.why: The Seer expresses messianic expectation of redemption in the child's lifetime.
The prediction concerns the final redemption of Judah and Jerusalem.

quotes: הראה באצבע עליו ואמר בימיו תוושע יהודה וירושלים
tags.why: The Seer discerns the child's future destiny.
The tsaddik's prediction did not come true, and the narrator explains this by the generation's sins.
As a child he stayed at the Seer's court in Lublin.
The scene is set at the Lublin court.

missing_concepts: a tsaddik's designation or blessing of a child's future greatness
messianic hope deferred because of sin
